stage: E3 full matrix (3 arms x 3 seeds, 300 GRPO steps)

eval.note: B3_s0 re-run at 3x512 for consistency (0.281, unchanged from 5x900 0.286)

gate2.rule: process arm beats B3 by > pooled across-seed SD on BOTH macro-F1 AND faithfulness

V2a.verdict: faithfulness PASS, accuracy narrow FAIL -> not met on strict rule

verdict: H1 SUPPORTED. V2b confirms Gate 2 (both metrics). V2a passes faithfulness decisively, borderline accuracy. Process-verified rewards beat outcome-only, most clearly on chain faithfulness; mechanism = dense reward wastes ~0% of rollout groups vs ~half for sparse outcome.

arm_definitions.V2a: dense step-level: base = mean(per-step verifiable rewards), final EXCLUDED
arm_definitions.V2b: dense step-level (StepGRPO-style): base = mean(per-step verifiable rewards + final)
arm_definitions.common: all arms add 0.25*format; only the per-step verification content of the base varies
arm_definitions.naming_correction: 'step-wise credit assignment' / 'per-step advantage attribution' RETRACTED. These arms do dense step-level REWARDING with a PATH-LEVEL group-normalized advantage — as does StepGRPO (R1-VL arXiv 2503.12937), which aggregates StepRAR+StepRVR step rewards into a scalar per-trajectory reward and normalizes it relative to the group (no token-level attribution). True per-step credit attribution is untested future work / optional E3 extension arm.
arm_definitions.differentiation_from_stepgrpo: StepGRPO's key steps are GPT-4-extracted (model-generated supervision); CoCr's step targets are deterministic from the source CIF via spglib/pymatgen — no model in the loop, so every step reward is programmatically verifiable rather than LLM-judged.

literature.zero_advantage: DAPO arXiv 2503.14476 (all-correct/all-wrong group -> zero advantage -> zero policy gradient; remedy = dynamic sampling filtering accuracy-0/1 prompts)
literature.our_orthogonal_contribution: a densely-verifiable reward prevents silent groups arising (~2%) rather than filtering them post hoc (~49% for outcome-only)

lattice_crosscheck.method: B3 per-rollout reward is 1.25 (correct) / 0.25 (wrong) when terminating, so group-mean reward = 0.25 + k/8; k=0 and k=8 are exactly the silent groups
lattice_crosscheck.conclusion: panel statistic confirmed two independent ways

closed_form_check.verdict: HOMOGENEOUS MODEL FAILS (~13x under-prediction) — the silent rate is NOT explained by mean accuracy

beta_binomial_fit.interpretation: a+b<1 => U-shaped per-prompt difficulty (mass near p~0 and p~1); PROMPT HETEROGENEITY, not mean accuracy, drives the sparsity

mechanism_analysis.dynamic_sampling_caution: documented failure mode on sparse hard-gated rewards: batch-wide rejection + resample thrashing (arXiv 2606.27210). With B3 at ~49% silent groups this is a live risk for the OUTCOME arm specifically. If adopted: cap resample rounds, log rejection rates, and apply to ALL arms or none — asymmetric adoption would break the matched-arm design.
